opportunities.label: opportunity
opportunities.title: Reduce CPU registry VM work with prepared execution kernels
opportunities.confidence: high for remaining work; medium for proposed solution
opportunities.hypothesis: The separate two-region trace still executes 106,479,261 VM calls, 3,603,641,198 node visits and 1,340,066,854 computed nodes. Prototype prepared branch/basic-block kernels or additional exact material certificates that eliminate traversal rather than assuming noise arithmetic is the whole cost. Compact dependencies, constant folding, bounded corner caches and high-Y material-zero proofs already exist. Do not resurrect the rejected identity-index shortcut as an established win.
opportunities.validation_plan: A/B process CPU work and wall time separately, scalar-reference all six roots, strict NBT on both seeds/dimensions/custom and 768-height packs. Preserve f32 order, lazy branches, implicit root zero, nonfinite failures and inclusive random endpoints. Retain only reproducible full-MCA improvements.

opportunities.label: opportunity
opportunities.title: Batch Nether dependency sampling across independent anchors
opportunities.confidence: high for stage concentration; medium for cause
opportunities.hypothesis: Nether CPU takes 25.64s and 116.60 CPU-seconds in this single early trial; vegetation/structure planning timers sum to 21.19s/13.26s. Metal still spends 2.54s in vegetation planning on a 2.93s region. Replay polls already batch within one anchor and memoize dependencies, but each GPU query batch synchronously locks feature_gpu. Measure batch sizes and repeated independent lookups, then coalesce compatible batches across anchors or reuse immutable results by complete dependency/version identity. Never cache solely by X/Z across edited prefixes.
opportunities.validation_plan: First collect one opt-in Nether anchor/query/lock-wait trace; several detailed worker probes are cfg(test), so zero release counters are not proof of no work. Separate locks, terrain dependencies, replay and GPU execution. Preserve root order/RNG state/version visibility and cancellation; exact NBT, seam/structure tests, bounded queue/memory and caller fairness.

opportunities.label: opportunity
opportunities.title: Make CPU lighting use bulk material rows and bounded reusable scratch
opportunities.expected_gain: medium; serial stage roughly 0.86–1.20s in warm CPU trials
opportunities.confidence: high for source/stage evidence; medium for speedup
opportunities.hypothesis: CPU lighting allocates dense materials/light/queue state per nonconstant tile and fetches each material through a scalar closure. Use existing Uniform/Dense row and section views, validated bulk fills and bounded scratch reuse. Compare tile cores 5/6/10: full nonconstant tiling stages 1,764/1,600/1,296 chunk equivalents for the 900-chunk interior; larger tiles also increase peak scratch and can lose constant-tile skips. Exact frontier seeding and constant tile elision already exist.
opportunities.validation_plan: Measure packing/initialization/propagation/output separately, not just a larger tile microbenchmark. Compare final complete MCA and exact integer lighting on transparent blocks, emitters, overhangs, Nether/End, custom heights and boundary rings. Keep original producer/consumer lanes runnable; do not add nested blocking Rayon dependencies or unbounded tile parallelism.

opportunities.label: opportunity
opportunities.title: Validate compact lighting and GPU palettes on Windows Vulkan
opportunities.expected_gain: high reduction in bytes; Windows speedup unknown
opportunities.confidence: high for byte reduction; low for Windows performance
opportunities.hypothesis: Metal defaults to compact input/output and GPU palettes; Vulkan and DX12 default to dense paths. The matched Metal ABBA control reduces lighting upload from 243.00 to 93.78 MiB, total upload from 249.69 to 100.58 MiB, and total readback from 143.66 to 113.65 MiB per region. Existing flags provide the experiment: RETINA_LIGHTING_INPUT=compact, RETINA_LIGHTING_OUTPUT=compact, RETINA_GPU_PALETTES=1. There is no new format to invent.
opportunities.validation_plan: On real Windows Vulkan, vary input, output and palettes separately before the combined setting. Fresh/repeated driver caches, representative NVIDIA/AMD adapters, Nether and tall packs, strict integer-light/NBT equivalence, transfer bytes, end-to-end throughput and peak memory. MoltenVK failure here cannot justify enabling defaults globally.

opportunities.label: opportunity
opportunities.title: Tune bounded region overlap around throughput, latency and memory
opportunities.expected_gain: medium; small sample suggests throughput upside
opportunities.hypothesis: Existing depth-two terrain and lighting pipelines already overlap submissions. In the matched 2-region ABBA test, one caller takes 0.640/0.967s per batch and two callers 0.573/0.520s. Two callers raise per-request latency and generation high-water RSS to about 1,738–1,747 MiB versus 1,485–1,544 MiB. Investigate host handoff bubbles and overlap encoding with ready work within current budgets, rather than simply raising caller counts.
opportunities.validation_plan: Repeat longer interleaved 1/2/4-caller trials at identical coordinates, completion boundaries and readiness. Record per-request p95, process CPU, interval-scoped GPU events, byte counts, RSS and fairness with foreground loads plus Chunky/DH. Require useful throughput gain without unacceptable memory/latency or starvation.

opportunities.label: opportunity
opportunities.title: Amortize chunk encoding/compressor scratch across lighting tiles
opportunities.expected_gain: medium for fast GPU generation; exact share unknown
opportunities.hypothesis: The lighting callback repeatedly creates parallel map_init scratch/compressor state; compression copies its reusable output into each retained Record. NBT/compression become more relevant when terrain is fast. Existing code already caches material NBT, handles uniform sections, uses libdeflate level 1, supports LZ4 and directly writes some GPU palette data. Profile scratch lifetime and allocation/copy cost before changing ownership or adding worker-retained buffers.
opportunities.validation_plan: Use allocation/CPU attribution with full lit-MCA output plus actual Minecraft read/decompress/decode. Benchmark existing zlib/LZ4 separately as a compatibility/size tradeoff; LZ4 is not a new feature. Preserve record limits, timestamps, partial-region preservation, atomic publication and bounded retained capacity. Summed parallel timers cannot be used as a serial speedup bound.

opportunities.label: opportunity
opportunities.title: Reduce definition-loading copies and unnecessary binding preparation
opportunities.expected_gain: medium for startup/memory; little steady-state benefit
opportunities.hypothesis: The loader retains the wire document and initialized profiles, clones structural profiles during decode, and constructs adapter metadata as another owned Value tree/JSON buffer. First binding registers every supported dimension. The measured load-and-bind range is about 0.7–4.0s in ordinary trials, strongly affected by host load; it includes metadata and preparation, not just disk IO. Profile these phases individually, then consider consuming conversions, shared immutable palette/metadata ownership and dimension-scoped preparation.
opportunities.validation_plan: Measure parse, validation, metadata construction/serialization, CPU preparation and registration separately on vanilla and the large pack. Keep retina.dat authoritative, full error validation and stable identities; lazy binding must not merely move the same stall to the first request or break retirement, concurrent binds, alternate execution/compression contracts or unsupported-dimension reporting.

opportunities.label: opportunity
opportunities.title: Make timeline attribution belong to the measured interval
opportunities.expected_gain: high decision value; no direct runtime gain claimed
opportunities.hypothesis: One Metal measurement lasts 648.6ms but its snapshot delta reports 2,483.7ms of device spans and 1,998.7ms of gaps. last_device_tick spans warmups/readiness waits and peak_in_flight is lifetime-wide. Concurrent spans can overlap and device gaps include copies/untracked work. These counters cannot be divided by batch wall time to claim GPU utilization or idle percentage.
opportunities.validation_plan: Add timestamp/event window membership and submission identities, explicitly account for boundary-crossing events and separate interval from lifetime peaks. Keep counter semantics documented and versioned. Validate warmup→readiness→measurement and overlapping terrain/material/lighting traces without synthetic preflight blockers; report measurement limitations instead of gating generation.

opportunities.label: opportunity
opportunities.title: Profile Java delivery and reuse Bukkit section bindings
opportunities.hypothesis: Bukkit already prebinds BlockData and caches chunk snapshots, but reconstructs canonical palette strings and resolves section BlockData arrays during installation. The generic FFI byte return also copies into Java. Investigate per-snapshot bound palettes/compact palette identities after actual host profiling. Native timings exclude Minecraft decoding, outer-ring seam lighting, live activation, rendering and packet delivery.
opportunities.validation_plan: Run the existing RegionDecodeBenchmark plus JFR for real server chunk loading/Bukkit generation, measuring allocation and main/IO-thread occupancy. Compare decoded values and block properties, plugin callback/thread requirements, unload lifetime and cache bounds. Do not call nested fixed-size voxel loops superlinear or remove bounded caches without evidence.

excluded_experiments: cpu-attribution is instrumented/sampled and heavily contended; use counts for work, not headline speed
metal-p2-1 through metal-p2-3 used an incomplete one-region reference; rerun with matched two-region baseline. No production NBT mismatch was observed.
vulkan-columns-1 and -2 used retired profile-zero requests; rejected by ownership validation. Replaced with actual saved procedural definitions.
Nether and End have one fresh process per backend; coverage observations, not stable distributions.
interpretation: All durations use completed lit-MCA zlib output. Each fresh MCA has 1024 generated, zero preserved records.
Warmups are excluded. Three warm CPU processes and three initial warm Metal processes use the same fixture/coordinate/budget but different host-load windows. No cross-backend precision speedup claim.
ABBA controls are small samples under shared host load; no default changes justified.
p95 values are descriptive small-sample percentiles, not population tail estimates.
CPU stages/recursive planning timers sum worker elapsed work and overlap; do not total them into host percentages. GPU spans/gaps may cross warmup/readiness boundaries; peaks are lifetime-wide.
Generation RSS is lifetime high-water through generation, includes startup/warmups and native pools; excludes later comparison/hash work. It is not per-region allocation or a leak measurement.
CPU/GPU NBT are not required to match each other; exact comparisons stay within a backend/control or retained CPU corpus.
Metal outer End uses CPU End substrate plus GPU lighting. Terrain pipeline completed=0, with positive lighting timestamps and transfer bytes; not an all-GPU End terrain measurement.
